layer3.original_text: If it is unavailable, incoming astronomical data will be lost.
layer3.refined_text: When the Correlator backend is unavailable, the backend system shall drop incoming astronomical data.
changes_made: Replaced the ambiguous pronoun 'it' with the specific domain term 'Correlator backend' to resolve the missing antecedent.
Replaced the predictive statement 'will be lost' with the mandatory normative modal and system action 'shall drop incoming astronomical data' adhering to EARS event-driven syntax.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The refinement strictly preserves the original technical scenario—that the unavailibility of the downstream processing/correlation component results in the dropping of incoming astronomical data—while replacing ambiguous phrasing and non-compliant modal verbs with precise EARS syntax and explicit domain vocabulary.

checks.observations: Successfully replaced the ambiguous pronoun 'it' with the defined domain term 'Correlator backend' and corrected the non-normative modal 'will' to 'shall'.
The terms 'Correlator backend', 'backend system', and 'incoming astronomical data' are clearly grounded in the project glossary and context without introducing subjective qualifiers.
No unwarranted protocols, APIs, or specific error-handling mechanisms were invented beyond what was implied by the original text.
The functional consequence (data loss when unavailable) is faithfully preserved using precise terminology ('drop incoming astronomical data').
Adheres to IEEE 29148 requirements syntax using the event-driven EARS pattern ('When [condition], the [system] shall [action]').
